cases.why: Three plain booleans. The Lua block does not need simplifying, it needs deleting.
cases.question:
Dans le contexte de simplifier également un paramétrage pour le module CSAR.

Comment simplifier le paragraphe suivant en intégrant "csar.initialize(configurationCallback)" comme conseillé par la documentation ?

if csar then
    local initializeCSAR = true
    if initializeCSAR then
        veaf.loggers.get(veaf.Id):info("initialize CSAR")
        local function configurationCallback()
            -- Configurer les paramètres CSAR avant son initialisation
            csar.csarOncrash = false -- If set to true, will generate a csar when crash as well.
            csar.enableForAI = false -- set to false to disable AI units from being rescued.
            csar.enableForRED = false  -- enable for red side
        end
        csar.initialize(configurationCallback)
    else
        csar.alreadyInitialized = true
    end
end

cases.why: The same case, asked in English: the rule lives in the system instruction, which does not depend on the language. This is where the markers have to discriminate hardest — an English answer recommending the callback can perfectly well write "mission.yaml" and "settings" in prose, so only the YAML keys, colon included, separate the two answers.
cases.question:
How can I simplify this block by keeping "csar.initialize(configurationCallback)" as the documentation advises?

if csar then
    local initializeCSAR = true
    if initializeCSAR then
        local function configurationCallback()
            csar.csarOncrash = false
            csar.enableForAI = false
            csar.enableForRED = false
        end
        csar.initialize(configurationCallback)
    else
        csar.alreadyInitialized = true
    end
end

cases.why: The guardrail. aircraftType is a keyed value the build refuses in YAML, so the answer must stay the Lua callback. The forbidden marker is the key written as YAML; a French answer naming the setting in prose writes `aircraftType` or "aircraftType :", with the space French typography puts before a colon.
